Benefit has been reported1 with the use of montelukast in patients with eosinophilic oesophagitis, a rare condition involving eosinophilic infiltration of the oesophagus with intermittent painful dysphagia. A systematic re- view with recommendations for the diagnosis and treatment of eosinophilic oesophagitis2 concluded that although leukotriene receptor antagonists had been shown to induce symptomatic re- lief at high doses, no significant improvements in histology were noted and their use for the treatment of eosinophilic oesophagitis is not supported by the current literature. 1.
